notes: The Housing Authority's first annual reports (1939-1943, bound together on IA) and its twentieth-anniversary report (1960). Curated: architects, contractors, contract prices and opening dates of the first public housing projects, and the 1950s projects' openings, onto the pages for their parcels. Holly Courts seeded.

coverage.remaining: Held or unplaced: Sunnydale (Albert F. Roller and Roland I. Stringham with Thomas Church; Barrett and Hilp; first tenants March 4, 1941) has no parcel in EAS; Potrero Terrace's other two lots (4222A001, 4223001) and Potrero Annex have no page; Yerba Buena Plaza and Annex, Harbor Slope, Hunters Point and Hayes Valley Apartments are demolished or unmatched; De Haro Plaza and Glen Crags were never built. Annual reports 1944-46 (war housing) not curated.

findings.description: The United States Housing Authority approved the Holly Park project here, San Francisco's first public housing, on vacant land the Board of Education had bought for a school it never built; an old fire station on the site was to be removed. Arthur Brown Jr. was its architect and L. Glenn Hall its landscape architect.

findings.address_as_written: Ping Yuen, Pacific Ave. & Powell St.
findings.description: Ping Yuen, Chinatown's first public housing, three buildings with 234 apartments on a site the Housing Authority had acquired and cleared before the war, was completed in late fall 1951 and dedicated with dragon, bands and firecrackers; all its first tenants were war veterans. Its Pailou gate copies the gate of the Yellow Monastery in Peking.

findings.address_as_written: Alice Griffith Garden Homes, Fitzgerald Ave. & Griffith St.
findings.description: Alice Griffith Garden Homes, row houses and three-story apartments for 354 families beside the new Candlestick Park, were under construction at an estimated $5,525,075, before the present buildings replaced them. They were named for an original Housing Commissioner who founded the Telegraph Hill Settlement House and the San Francisco Planning and Urban Renewal Association.
